title: Emergent Topology from Nonlocal Electronic Correlations in One Dimension
authors: Félix Fossati, Erik Linnér, Evgeny A. Stepanov
abstract: We demonstrate that electronic correlations in low-dimensional systems can induce topological phases starting from a topologically trivial noninteracting band structure. Using an advanced cluster-diagrammatic many-body approach applied to the one-dimensional extended Hubbard model, we show that tuning the nonlocal Coulomb interaction drives the emergence of bond-order-wave (BOW) and charge-density-wave (CDW) phases. Despite being interaction-driven and symmetry-broken, these states admit an effective low-energy single-particle description. In particular, the BOW phase maps onto an effective Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, while the CDW phase, with subleading bond-order correlations, corresponds to a Rice-Mele model. Both phases exhibit a nontrivial topological character, manifested by the presence of localized edge states. Our results establish a mechanism by which nonlocal electronic correlations generate emergent topology in correlated systems.
summary: The authors demonstrate that nonlocal electronic correlations in 1D materials can spontaneously generate topological order by inducing Charge-Density-Wave (CDW) or Bond-Order-Wave (BOW) states. Using advanced cluster diagrammatic techniques, they map these interacting many-body phases onto effective Hamiltonians resembling the SSH and Rice-Mele models, confirming their nontrivial topological nature via edge state signatures.
main_problem: The study aims to establish a mechanism by which nonlocal electronic correlations can induce topological phases in low-dimensional systems, starting from an initially trivial noninteracting band structure.
main_result: Nonlocal interactions drive the system into Bond-Order-Wave (BOW) and Charge-Density-Wave (CDW) phases, both of which possess nontrivial topological character, evidenced by localized edge states.
method: The research employs an advanced cluster-diagrammatic many-body approach (D-TRILEX framework) applied to the extended Hubbard model, mapping the interacting system onto effective noninteracting Hamiltonians for analysis.
model_or_system: The physical system is modeled by the one-dimensional extended Hubbard model, characterized by hopping ($t$), local repulsion ($U$), and nearest-neighbor nonlocal repulsion ($V$). The analysis focuses on the emergence of BOW and CDW phases.
key_observables: BOW order parameter ($	ext{O}_{	ext{BOW}}$), staggered charge density ($	ext{O}_{	ext{CDW}}$), effective Hamiltonian parameters ($u_k, v_k, w_k$), and edge-localization weight $|\phi_j^{	ext{edge}}|^2$.
important_parameters: Nonlocal interaction strength ($V$) relative to local repulsion ($U$); temperature ($T=0.1$).
main_assumptions: The single-site D-TRILEX approach fails for symmetry-broken phases due to the nonlocal nature of the order parameters, necessitating a dimer/cluster formulation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing coexisting CDW+BOW regions; energy spectra demonstrate the evolution from bulk states to SSH-like edge modes (BOW) and finally to RM-like gapped states (CDW).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the model and using cluster methods to identify symmetry-broken phases. It then maps these interacting states onto effective single-particle Hamiltonians, analyzing the topological signatures (edge states) associated with both CDW and BOW order parameters.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical link between interaction-driven symmetry breaking in correlated electron models and the emergence of robust topological invariants, which is highly relevant for understanding novel quantum phases in condensed matter systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The U-V phase diagram of the half-filled 1D extended Hub- bard model obtained at T = 0.1 using D-TRILEX. The CDW phase boundaries calculated within the single-site and dimer frameworks are shown in dashed and solid red curves, respectively. The mean- field estimate for the CDW transition V = U/2 is given by the dashed black line. The BOW phase boundary obtained in the dimer calcula- tion is depicted by the yellow curve.

FIG. 2. Evolution of the CDW (blue markers) and BOW (red mark- ers) order parameters with nonlocal interaction V. The results are ob- tained within the dimer D-TRILEX approach for U = 1.5 (top panel) and U = 3.0 (bottom panel). The curvature κ of the BOW curve is shown in orange. VCDW c (dotted vertical blue line) marks the CDW onset. VBOW c (dashed vertical red line) corresponds to the maximum of κ(V) before the CDW sets in and is present only at U = 1.5.

FIG. 3. Energy spectrum of Heff for a 64-site chain with open boundary conditions obtained as a function of V at U = 1.5. For clarity reasons, only a representative subset of the low-energy levels are shown and intermediate values of V are removed. Each triangle marker represents a single eigenstate: its orientation encodes the sub- lattice polarization P(n), and its color encodes the edge-localization weight |ϕ(n)|2 edge, from bulk-extended (yellow) to boundary-localized (red to black). Vertical dashed lines mark VBOW c and VCDW c .
